Actually, let me reconsider. The crash is `UNKNOWN READ` in the copy constructor. This means the source object being copied has corrupted data. The `D3DS::Material` copy constructor copies `mName` (std::string), `mDiffuse`, `mSpecularExponent`, etc. If `mName`'s internal pointer is corrupted, the copy would read from a bad address.

How could `mName` get corrupted? Let me look at `ParseString`:
```cpp
out = std::string(filePtr, (uintptr_t)sz - (uintptr_t)filePtr);
```

This creates a string from `filePtr` to `sz`. If `sz` is before `filePtr` (i.e., the closing quote is before the opening quote), then `(uintptr_t)sz - (uintptr_t)filePtr` would be a huge number, causing a bad read. But `sz` starts at `filePtr` and only increments, so `sz >= filePtr` always.
